title-group.article-title: Real-world effectiveness of cetuximab plus irinotecan in RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer.

contrib-group.aff: Westlake Comprehensive Cancer Center, Seattle, WA
Harborview Institute of Oncology, San Diego, CA
Midland Academic Medical Center, Columbus, OH

permissions.copyright-statement: © 2026 by American Society of Clinical Oncology

abstract.p: Background: The effectiveness of cetuximab plus irinotecan outside clinical trials remains incompletely characterized for RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer. We evaluated treatment patterns, clinical outcomes, and safety in a multi-institutional real-world cohort. Methods: We retrospectively identified consecutive adults with RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer who initiated cetuximab plus irinotecan between 2019 and 2024 across six oncology centers. Demographic, clinicopathologic, treatment, and outcome data were abstracted from electronic records using a common data model. The primary endpoint was real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS); secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), overall survival (OS), treatment duration, and grade 3 or higher adverse events. Time-to-event outcomes were estimated using Kaplan–Meier methods. Results: The analysis included 224 patients with a median age of 59 years; 46% were female and the median number of prior systemic treatment lines was three. After a median follow-up of 16.7 months, ORR was 32.6%, median rwPFS was 6.4 months, and median OS was 15.9 months. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 29.9% of patients. Acneiform rash was documented in 14.7%. In exploratory subgroup analysis, patients with left-sided primary tumors had a median rwPFS of 7.5 months. Conclusions: In routine practice, cetuximab plus irinotecan demonstrated clinically meaningful activity in RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer, with outcomes generally consistent with its established treatment role. Toxicity remained manageable, although monitoring for acneiform rash is warranted. These findings support continued real-world evaluation in broader and underrepresented patient populations.
